insights.insight: Static source can expose a plausible state path without establishing that the integrated product actually exhibits the defect; route to the cheapest integrated discriminator before granting build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: Already encoded by discrimination-before-redesign and reality-floor rules. OSS-0007 is a useful neighbor: a directly visible guard-contract asymmetry can justify a narrow reversible build at R1 without waiting for field evidence. OSS-0013 exercises the same boundary in HOLDOUT and remains score-only until the wave closes.

insights.insight: Independent evidence about a neighboring bug or the same component can support a failure family without confirming the exact mechanism under adjudication.
insights.promotion_reason: Recurring adjudication hazard, but still lacks an executable positive-control gate and closed holdout wave. BATCH-007 adds two more examples: Butterfly file-loss evidence does not confirm newer-file compatibility policy, and Linkwarden preservation failures do not confirm collection-delete rollback inconsistency.

insights.insight: A suspicious timing workaround is not itself permission to refactor; first reproduce the event mechanism with and without the workaround.
insights.promotion_reason: Single case, no neighbor control, no positive control and no HOLDOUT evidence.

insights.insight: A repository can establish exactly what the product does while remaining unable to establish that the behavior is a defect; when the unresolved question is intended interaction/configuration policy, route to OWNER instead of converting implementation certainty into build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: Already encoded by Neta's evidence/authority/permission separation. OSS-0012 extends the same boundary to destructive recovery policy: irreversibility does not itself authorize automatic undo. OSS-0008 remains HOLDOUT score-only.

insights.insight: When a product contract is explicit and equivalent controls already enforce it, one unguarded sibling path can justify a narrow reversible consistency fix without asserting any field outcome.
insights.promotion_reason: OSS-0014 exposes the missing boundary in this family: sibling equivalence is not itself an explicit product contract. Actual Budget's confirmation-versus-undo tradeoff was OWNER-owned, so asymmetry alone could not grant BUILD permission. This family now needs a sharper gate before any promotion.

insights.insight: Source can prove that a warning, recovery gesture, or affordance exists; it cannot prove that people notice, understand, or successfully use it. Adequacy claims about discoverability or error prevention require FIELD evidence rather than additional UI by default.
insights.promotion_reason: This is a concrete transfer instance of the existing R6/field-outcome rule, not a new heuristic. OSS-0010 independently exercises the same boundary in HOLDOUT and is score-only until the wave closes.

insights.insight: Equivalent-looking sibling paths do not establish a shared product contract. Before turning asymmetry into BUILD permission, distinguish an explicit invariant from a consistency preference or interaction-policy tradeoff that belongs to OWNER.
insights.promotion_reason: OSS-0018 strengthens the missing judgment identified by OSS-0014: the same control surface can legitimately apply different guards when the underlying consequences differ. Historical field evidence supported confirmation for irreversible playlist deletion but not reversible unsave. The candidate still lacks an executable discrimination gate, deliberate red positive control and unseen HOLDOUT success, so it remains memory only.

insights.insight: Static source can show a recovery promise and recovery machinery but cannot establish the operational guarantee that support or a deployed environment can actually deliver. Calibrate such promises from an ENVIRONMENT/support drill rather than from UI reachability alone.
insights.promotion_reason: A concrete transfer instance of the canonical reality/authority separation. It adds ENVIRONMENT evidence but does not justify a new heuristic.

insights.insight: A database transaction does not make external filesystem, search-index, network, or other side effects atomic. When a decision depends on rollback consistency across authorities, explicitly identify the external side-effect boundary and leave a failure-injection gate before treating the repair as proven.
insights.promotion_reason: The static code clearly exposes a cross-boundary atomicity risk, but post-freeze issue evidence did not reproduce the exact rollback inconsistency. Keep as technical case memory until a deliberate failure-injection fixture can turn red and a neighboring safe transaction boundary is available as control.

decision_modes.note: All target routing modes remain represented. BATCH-007 adds no new mode and therefore contributes through boundary testing rather than mode discovery.

failure_families.note: I-009 is a new memory-only technical family around false atomicity across external side effects. It is not a promotion candidate because the exact failure remains unreproduced.

authority_boundaries.note: No new Neta authority error in BATCH-007. Butterfly remains an unresolved OWNER-policy boundary; Super Productivity confirms a REPO-local operational invariant.

baseline_decision_deltas.note: No fully surviving decision delta was added in BATCH-007. This is retained as a negative/marginal-information result rather than rescued by counting findings.

protocol_warning: Earlier candidate-selection contamination remains quarantined: Kanboard and Vikunja were excluded after metadata/history exposure. During BATCH-004 Kanboard was initially reconsidered, but the existing warning was detected before case creation and it was excluded again. Volmarg/personal-management-system was rejected before case assignment because its pinned repository is backend-only. BATCH-005 excluded meetfranz/franz after the README established that the repository is an inactive predecessor, and excluded WeekToDo because its last push fell outside the 12-month activity window. BATCH-006 pinned all three repositories through git refs before Phase B and exposed no issue/PR history until after Neta and baseline outputs were frozen. In BATCH-007, the existing Franz and Vikunja exclusions were re-detected before case creation and honored. sissbruecker/linkding was also quarantined before case creation because a Phase-B code-search result exposed a CHANGELOG history snippet. Butterfly, Linkwarden and Super Productivity entered the batch with pinned refs and no issue bodies opened before their Phase B/C decisions were frozen.
